# jammi_encoders::aggregate - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-encoders/0.32.1/jammi_encoders/aggregate/index.html

## Expand description

Differentiable segment-aggregate: reduce a `[N, D]` value tensor into a
`[num_segments, D]` tensor by folding each row into the segment its id names,
with full autograd support.

This is the train-time twin of the data-plane vector-aggregation UDAF
(`vector_mean` / `vector_sum` / `vector_max`): one pooling semantics, two
execution contexts. The UDAF folds f64 accumulators over arbitrary SQL group
keys and serves a result table; this folds an f32 candle [ Tensor](https://docs.rs/candle-core/0.9.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/candle_core/tensor/struct.Tensor.html) over
dense

`0..num_segments` ids inside an autograd graph so the same pooling can
be a differentiable layer.[§](https://docs.rs#parity-with-the-udaf-and-the-one-deliberate-divergence)Parity with the UDAF, and the one deliberate divergence

The two paths agree row-by-row within f32-vs-f64 rounding **except** on the
empty-segment convention, which cannot agree by construction: a candle
tensor has no per-row null, so where the UDAF emits a *null* vector for a
group with no rows, this emits a **zero** row. Zero is NaN-free,
deterministic, and differentiable (an all-empty input still backprops),
which a null cannot be. The divergence is intentional and is the only point
where the two pooling implementations differ; everything else (the lane fold,
permutation-invariance, mean’s divide-at-finalise, max’s lane-wise reduction)
matches.

[§](https://docs.rs#index-domain)Index domain

`segment_ids` must be dense (`0..num_segments`) — mapping arbitrary keys to
dense ids is the caller’s job and is the parity surface between this and the
UDAF’s SQL `GROUP BY`. Ids out of `0..num_segments` are a caller error
surfaced by the underlying gather/scatter, not silently dropped.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Segment](https://docs.rs/enum.SegmentReduce.html)- Reduce
- The element-wise reduction `segment_aggregate`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [l2_](https://docs.rs/fn.l2_normalize_rows.html)- normalize_ - rows
- L2-normalise each row of a `[num_segments, D]`(or any`[.., D]`) tensor along the last axis, matching the encoders’ pooled-embedding normalisation. Exposed because a segment-pooled embedding is normalised the same way a token-pooled one is.
- [segment_](https://docs.rs/fn.segment_aggregate.html)- aggregate
- Reduce `values`(`[N, D]`, f32) into`[num_segments, D]`by folding row`n`into segment`segment_ids[n]`, differentiably.

---

# jammi_encoders::audio - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-encoders/0.32.1/jammi_encoders/audio/index.html

## Expand description

Closed-enum dispatch over the audio encoder families used by `jammi-ai`.

Parallel to the text-side [ crate::any::AnyEncoder](https://docs.rs/enum.AnyEncoder.html): a family-erased
handle so callers can hold any supported audio encoder without trait-object
overhead. Every audio encoder maps a 4-channel CLAP fusion spectrogram

`[batch, 4, time, num_mel_bins]` to pooled shared-latent embeddings
`[batch, embedding_dim]`, and reports the mel-bin count the spectrogram must
carry. The bytes-to-spectrogram front-end geometry (sample rate, FFT size,
hop, window length) is a feature-extractor concern owned by the caller’s
`ClapFrontendConfig`, not the tower — the tower consumes the packed features
and is agnostic to how they were produced.## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [AnyAudio](https://docs.rs/enum.AnyAudioEncoder.html)- Encoder
- Family-erased audio encoder for callers that need to hand around any of the supported audio encoder types without trait-object overhead.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Audio](https://docs.rs/trait.AudioEncoder.html)- Encoder
- The contract every audio encoder satisfies: 4-channel fusion spectrogram in, pooled L2-normalized embedding out, plus the mel-bin count the input must carry so the front-end can be config-driven.

# jammi_encoders::bert - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-encoders/0.32.1/jammi_encoders/bert/index.html

## Expand description

BERT-family encoder (BERT, RoBERTa, CamemBERT, XLM-RoBERTa).

Mirrors candle-transformers’ `BertModel` architecture so the parity test
can numerically verify the frozen forward pass against the upstream
implementation. The six attention/FFN linears per layer (`query`, `key`,
`value`, `attention.output.dense`, `intermediate.dense`, `output.dense`)
are wrapped in [ jammi_lora::MaybeLoraLinear](https://docs.rs/jammi-lora/0.32.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jammi_lora/wrapper/enum.MaybeLoraLinear.html) so a builder-time

[selects which of them carry trainable adapters.](https://docs.rs/jammi-lora/0.32.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jammi_lora/config/struct.LoraBuildConfig.html)

`jammi_lora::LoraBuildConfig`Two safetensors layouts are supported transparently:

- Raw `BertModel`checkpoints — keys at the root (`embeddings.word_embeddings.weight`).
- `BertForX`checkpoints — keys under a- `"bert."`prefix.

Detection is via a single `contains_tensor` probe at build time.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Bert](https://docs.rs/struct.Bert.html)
- BERT / RoBERTa / CamemBERT / XLM-RoBERTa encoder with optional LoRA adapters
on the six per-layer linears (`query`,`key`,`value`,`attention.output.dense`,`intermediate.dense`,`output.dense`).
- [Bert](https://docs.rs/struct.BertBuilder.html)- Builder
- Fluent builder for `Bert``Bert::builder`
- [Bert](https://docs.rs/struct.BertConfig.html)- Config
- Architecture configuration deserialised from a HuggingFace `config.json`.

# jammi_encoders::clip_text - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-encoders/0.32.1/jammi_encoders/clip_text/index.html

## Expand description

OpenCLIP text transformer.

Loads weights from OpenCLIP safetensors checkpoints under their native
key layout (`token_embedding.weight`, `positional_embedding`,
`transformer.resblocks.{n}.attn.in_proj_weight`, …, `ln_final.*`,
`text_projection`).

The text tower is causally masked (lower-triangular attention), uses
QuickGelu in the MLP, pools by selecting the hidden state at the EOT
position (the argmax of the input token IDs along the sequence axis),
projects the pooled state through `text_projection` into the shared
CLIP latent space, and L2-normalizes the result.

Forward output is `[batch, embed_dim]` in the same latent space as
[ crate::clip_text::ClipTextConfig::embed_dim](https://docs.rs/struct.ClipTextConfig.html#structfield.embed_dim) vision-tower outputs,
enabling cross-modal cosine similarity.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Clip](https://docs.rs/struct.ClipText.html)- Text
- OpenCLIP text transformer.
- [Clip](https://docs.rs/struct.ClipTextConfig.html)- Text - Config
- Architecture configuration for the OpenCLIP text transformer.

---

# jammi_encoders::context - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-encoders/0.32.1/jammi_encoders/context/index.html

## Expand description

The amortized in-context predictor family — `AnyContextPredictor` — the
learned-aggregation point of the neural-process spectrum.

Each member conditions on a *context set* (retrieved neighbour features and
their outcomes) and emits a predictive-distribution head at a target, in one
differentiable forward pass. The three curated members are a closed enum,
the same curation bar and tier boundary as [ crate::AnyEncoder](https://docs.rs/enum.AnyEncoder.html): a consumer
selects a member by config, never authors a novel architecture through it.

- `Cnp`- `crate::segment_aggregate`
- `AttnCnp`
- `Tnp`- `(context ∪ target)`token set; the strongest member, the prior-fitted-network point.

Every member’s `forward` returns the *same* `[B, head_width]` float head as
the distributional output adapter consumes: `head_width = 2` for a Gaussian
`(mean, raw_std)`, `head_width = levels` for a quantile head. One output
shape, three architectures behind it.

[§](https://docs.rs#context-representation--the-contextepisode-input)Context representation — the `ContextEpisode`

`ContextEpisode`The three members want the context in two natural forms, and the input type carries the one representation from which both derive, so a caller assembles it once:

- a **dense**`[B, k, feature_dim]`/`[B, k, value_dim]`form with a`[B, k]`presence mask, padded to the per-batch maximum`k`. AttnCnp and Tnp attend over this with an additive mask (built from the presence mask via the crate-internal`extended_attention_mask`) so a padded member receives zero attention weight — never attended over.
- a **ragged**form — the masked-in members flattened to`[N, …]`with a`[N]`segment-id mapping each to its episode`0..B`.`Cnp``crate::segment_aggregate`

An *empty* context (`k == 0`, or an episode whose whole row is masked) is
NaN-free for every member: Cnp pools to the documented zero row, AttnCnp
routes through a learned prior path, Tnp attends over the lone target token.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [AttnCnp](https://docs.rs/struct.AttnCnp.html)
- Attentive CNP: target-query × context-key/value cross-attention pooling → ρ.
- [Cnp](https://docs.rs/struct.Cnp.html)
- Conditional Neural Process: φ (per-member) → segment-mean pool → ρ → head.
- [Context](https://docs.rs/struct.ContextEpisode.html)- Episode
- A target row plus its (padded) context set — the input to every predictor’s
`forward`. See the[module docs](https://docs.rs/index.html)for the dual dense/ragged representation and why this single type serves all three members.
- [Context](https://docs.rs/struct.ContextPredictorConfig.html)- Predictor - Config
- Configuration for an `AnyContextPredictor`
- [Tnp](https://docs.rs/struct.Tnp.html)
- Transformer Neural Process: token the context ∪ target, self-attend, decode the target token.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [AnyContext](https://docs.rs/enum.AnyContextPredictor.html)- Predictor
- Family-erased in-context predictor: a closed enum over the three curated
architectures, mirroring `crate::AnyEncoder`
- [Context](https://docs.rs/enum.ContextArchitecture.html)- Architecture
- Which curated in-context-predictor architecture a `ContextPredictorConfig`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [attention_](https://docs.rs/fn.attention_weights.html)- weights
- The softmax attention *weights*`softmax(QKᵀ/√d + key_mask)`for the single-head case (`num_heads == 1`), shape`[B, q_len, kv_len]`.
- [multi_](https://docs.rs/fn.multi_head_attention.html)- head_ - attention
- Multi-head scaled dot-product attention of a query set against a key/value
set: `softmax(QKᵀ/√d + key_mask)·V`, recombined across heads.

---

# jammi_encoders::distilbert - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-encoders/0.32.1/jammi_encoders/distilbert/index.html

## Expand description

DistilBERT encoder with built-in PEFT support via [ jammi_lora](https://docs.rs/jammi-lora/0.32.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jammi_lora/index.html).

Mirrors candle-transformers’ `models::distilbert::DistilBertModel` in
structure, with the following per-spec differences from BERT:

- No `token_type_embeddings`— embeddings are word + position only.
- Attention linears are named `q_lin`/`k_lin`/`v_lin`/`out_lin`.
- FFN linears are named `lin1`(dim → hidden_dim) and`lin2`(hidden_dim → dim).
- Per-layer LayerNorms are `sa_layer_norm`(post-attention) and`output_layer_norm`(post-FFN).
- Weight prefix in the safetensors archive is `"distilbert."`.
- Post-LayerNorm architecture (residual then LayerNorm).
- Activation is `gelu_erf`.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Distil](https://docs.rs/struct.DistilBert.html)- Bert
- DistilBERT sentence encoder with selective LoRA adapters on attention and FFN linears.
- [Distil](https://docs.rs/struct.DistilBertBuilder.html)- Bert - Builder
- Builder for `DistilBert``DistilBert::builder`
- [Distil](https://docs.rs/struct.DistilBertConfig.html)- Bert - Config
- DistilBERT architecture configuration.

# jammi_encoders::htsat_audio - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-encoders/0.32.1/jammi_encoders/htsat_audio/index.html

## Expand description

HTSAT-Swin CLAP audio tower.

The audio tower of a CLAP (Contrastive Language-Audio Pretraining) model in
the HuggingFace `ClapAudioModelWithProjection` lineage: an HTSAT
(Hierarchical Token-Semantic Audio Transformer) built on a Swin-Transformer
spine. It consumes a fused 4-channel log-mel spectrogram
`[batch, 4, time, freq]`, batch-normalizes it, bicubic-resamples the time
axis up to the Swin input width, reshapes the time-frequency plane into a
square “image”, and patch-embeds it. The patch embedding is gated per sample
by `is_longer`: a longer clip’s embedding is the Attentional-Feature-Fusion
(AFF) blend of the global patch-conv and the local mel channels, while a
short clip uses the global patch-conv alone.

This module implements the complete tower: the front half (batch-norm →
bicubic time-resample → `reshape_mel2img` → fused patch-embed) through the
`patch_embed` boundary, the four-stage Swin spine (W-MSA / SW-MSA blocks with
recomputed relative-position bias and shift-window masks, plus patch-merging
downsamples), the final LayerNorm and group-2D pooling, and the projection
head with L2-normalization producing the shared-latent audio embedding.

Weight keys follow the HF safetensors layout. The encoder modules live under
`audio_model.audio_encoder.*` (built from
`vb.pp("audio_model").pp("audio_encoder")`); the projection head lives at
`audio_projection.*`, a sibling of `audio_model`. [ HtsatAudio::load](https://docs.rs/struct.HtsatAudio.html#method.load) takes
the safetensors root and wires both.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Clap](https://docs.rs/struct.ClapAudioProjection.html)- Audio - Projection
- The CLAP audio projection head: `linear1 → act → linear2`, then L2-normalize.
- [Front](https://docs.rs/struct.FrontHalf.html)- Half
- The per-boundary activations produced while running the front half, captured so the caller (parity harness) can gate every unit against its golden.
- [Htsat](https://docs.rs/struct.HtsatAudio.html)- Audio
- The full HTSAT-Swin CLAP audio tower: encoder spine + projection head, returning the L2-normalized shared-latent embedding.
- [Htsat](https://docs.rs/struct.HtsatAudioConfig.html)- Audio - Config
- Architecture configuration for the HTSAT-Swin CLAP audio tower, deserialized
from a HuggingFace `ClapAudioConfig`(`config.json`or the`audio_config`block of a top-level CLAP config).
- [Htsat](https://docs.rs/struct.HtsatAudioEncoder.html)- Audio - Encoder
- HTSAT-Swin CLAP audio encoder — front half (through `patch_embed`) plus the full Swin spine, final LayerNorm, and group-2D pooling.
- [Spine](https://docs.rs/struct.Spine.html)
- The per-boundary activations produced while running the Swin spine, captured
so the parity harness can gate every unit against its golden. `blocks[s][b]`is stage`s`block`b`’s output;`downsamples[s]`is stage`s`’s patch-merging output (`None`for the final stage).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [l2_](https://docs.rs/fn.l2_normalize.html)- normalize
- L2-normalize each row of a `[B, D]`tensor along the last axis (`F.normalize(p=2, dim=-1, eps=1e-12)`).

# jammi-lora 0.32.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/jammi-lora/0.32.1

# jammi-lora

Static-dispatch PEFT-style LoRA primitives for [candle](https://github.com/huggingface/candle). Closed-enum
dispatch, immutable construction, native to candle `0.9.x`.

`jammi-lora` gives you everything you need to add LoRA adapters to a candle
model — `LoraLinear`, a `MaybeLoraLinear` wrapper, build helpers, adapter
metadata, and safetensors persistence — without proc-macros and without trait
objects in the forward path.

## Status

`0.x` — pre-stable. The on-disk adapter format (`adapter_config.json` +
`adapter.safetensors`) is stable for the `0.x` line.

## Quick start

```
use HashMap;
use ;
use ;
use ;
let device = Cpu;
let varmap = new;
let vb = from_varmap;
// A frozen base linear from your model.
let base_weight = zeros.unwrap;
let base = new;
// Wrap it with a LoRA adapter (rank 4, alpha 8, ZerosB init).
let lora = new_simple.unwrap;
let layer = Lora;
let x = randn.unwrap;
let _y = layer.forward.unwrap;
```
## Public API

- [`LoraLinear`] — single LoRA-augmented linear layer.
- [`MaybeLoraLinear`] —`enum { Frozen(Linear), Lora(LoraLinear) }`. Match on it in your model so dispatch stays compile-time-inlined.
- [`LoraBuildConfig`] — borrowed-reference build configuration.
- [`should_apply_lora`] / [`effective_rank`] — module-name matching helpers that mirror HuggingFace PEFT's`target_modules`/`rank_pattern`semantics.
- [`AdapterConfig`] / [`BackboneDtype`] — persisted adapter metadata.
- [`save_adapter`] / [`load_adapter`] — safetensors-based directory persistence.
- [`LoraInitMode`] — A/B init strategy (`ZerosB`default,`Gaussian`).
- [`LoraError`] — single error type for the whole crate.

## When to use this crate

Use `jammi-lora` when you need LoRA adapters on candle `0.9.x` with:

- compile-time dispatch (no `Box<dyn …>`in the forward path),
- a small, focused surface (one enum, one struct, a builder helper),
- HuggingFace PEFT-compatible `target_modules`/`rank_pattern`semantics,
- a stable on-disk adapter format.

If you want broader model coverage, multi-adapter switching, or proc-macro
sugar, consider [candle-lora](https://github.com/EricLBuehler/candle-lora).

---

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [effective_](https://docs.rs/fn.effective_rank.html)- rank
- Effective LoRA rank for `module_name`: consult`rank_pattern`for the first substring match, falling back to`default_rank`.
- [load_](https://docs.rs/fn.load_adapter.html)- adapter
- Read a LoRA adapter directory: parses `adapter_config.json`into`C`and loads`adapter.safetensors`onto`device`.
- [save_](https://docs.rs/fn.save_adapter.html)- adapter
- Write a LoRA adapter to `dir`:
- [should_](https://docs.rs/fn.should_apply_lora.html)- apply_ - lora
- Decide whether a linear layer at `layer_idx`with name suffix`module_name`should receive a LoRA adapter.

# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-lora/0.32.1/src/jammi_lora/lib.rs.html

# jammi_lora/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! Static-dispatch PEFT-style LoRA primitives for [candle].
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! The crate exposes everything needed to add LoRA adapters to a candle-based
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! model without proc-macros or trait objects:
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//!
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! - [`LoraLinear`] — a single LoRA-augmented linear layer.
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! - [`MaybeLoraLinear`] — closed-enum dispatch between a plain `Linear` and a
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//!   [`LoraLinear`], so a model can be parameterised at construction and stays
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//!   inlinable at every forward call.
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! - [`LoraBuildConfig`] / [`should_apply_lora`] / [`effective_rank`] —
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//!   call-site decisions about which modules receive an adapter and at what
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//!   rank.
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! - [`AdapterConfig`] + [`save_adapter`] / [`load_adapter`] — adapter
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//!   directory persistence.
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//!
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! [candle]: https://github.com/huggingface/candle
[17](https://docs.rs#17)
[18](https://docs.rs#18)mod adapter;
[19](https://docs.rs#19)mod config;
[20](https://docs.rs#20)mod init;
[21](https://docs.rs#21)// The candle-backed primitives, their error type, and persistence. Gated behind
[22](https://docs.rs#22)// the default-on `candle` feature so a config-vocabulary-only consumer (one that
[23](https://docs.rs#23)// needs `FineTuneConfig`'s field types but never a tensor) pulls no candle stack.
[24](https://docs.rs#24)// `LoraError`'s every constructor lives in these modules, so it rides the gate too.
[25](https://docs.rs#25)#[cfg(feature = "candle")]
[26](https://docs.rs#26)mod error;
[27](https://docs.rs#27)#[cfg(feature = "candle")]
[28](https://docs.rs#28)mod lora_linear;
[29](https://docs.rs#29)#[cfg(feature = "candle")]
[30](https://docs.rs#30)mod save_load;
[31](https://docs.rs#31)// Seeded, candle-RNG-free init and dropout for the LoRA path. Only the
[32](https://docs.rs#32)// candle-backed `lora_linear` consumes it, so it rides the same feature gate.
[33](https://docs.rs#33)#[cfg(feature = "candle")]
[34](https://docs.rs#34)mod seeded;
[35](https://docs.rs#35)#[cfg(feature = "candle")]
[36](https://docs.rs#36)mod wrapper;
[37](https://docs.rs#37)
[38](https://docs.rs#38)pub use adapter::{AdapterConfig, BackboneDtype};
[39](https://docs.rs#39)pub use config::{effective_rank, should_apply_lora, LoraBuildConfig};
[40](https://docs.rs#40)#[cfg(feature = "candle")]
[41](https://docs.rs#41)pub use error::LoraError;
[42](https://docs.rs#42)pub use init::LoraInitMode;
[43](https://docs.rs#43)#[cfg(feature = "candle")]
[44](https://docs.rs#44)pub use lora_linear::LoraLinear;
[45](https://docs.rs#45)#[cfg(feature = "candle")]
[46](https://docs.rs#46)pub use save_load::{load_adapter, save_adapter};
[47](https://docs.rs#47)#[cfg(feature = "candle")]
[48](https://docs.rs#48)pub use wrapper::MaybeLoraLinear;

# MaybeLoraLinear in jammi_lora - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-lora/0.32.1/jammi_lora/enum.MaybeLoraLinear.html

```
pub enum MaybeLoraLinear {
    Frozen(
```
[Linear](https://docs.rs/candle-nn/0.9.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/candle_nn/linear/struct.Linear.html)),
    Lora([LoraLinear](https://docs.rs/struct.LoraLinear.html)),
}## Expand description

Either a frozen `candle_nn::Linear` or a LoRA-augmented one.

Construction is the only place callers decide which arm applies; once built,
the rest of the model holds an opaque `MaybeLoraLinear` and forwards through
it without branching.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Frozen)

### Frozen([Linear](https://docs.rs/candle-nn/0.9.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/candle_nn/linear/struct.Linear.html))

Plain frozen linear — no LoRA adapter installed.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Lora)

### Lora([LoraLinear](https://docs.rs/struct.LoraLinear.html))

Frozen base wrapped with a trainable LoRA A/B path.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Dispatch the forward pass to the appropriate variant.

The `Frozen` arm casts the input to the weight’s dtype so the underlying
matmul sees matching precisions — this matters when a BF16 backbone is
driven by an F32 input.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/jammi_lora/wrapper.rs.html#46-51)#### pub fn [trainable_params](https://docs.rs#method.trainable_params)(&self) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<&[Tensor](https://docs.rs/candle-core/0.9.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/candle_core/tensor/struct.Tensor.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/jammi_lora/wrapper.rs.html#46-51)

#### pub fn [trainable_params](https://docs.rs#method.trainable_params)(&self) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<&[Tensor](https://docs.rs/candle-core/0.9.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/candle_core/tensor/struct.Tensor.html)>

Trainable parameters of this layer. Empty for `Frozen`; the LoRA A and
B tensors for `Lora`.

Export the LoRA A and B tensors keyed as `{prefix}.lora_a` /
`{prefix}.lora_b`, moved to CPU for safetensors serialisation.
Returns an empty map for `Frozen`.

Restore the LoRA A and B tensors from a `{prefix}.lora_a` /
`{prefix}.lora_b` pair in `weights`. Missing keys are silently ignored
— the caller controls which prefixes they expect to populate. No-op on
`Frozen`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/jammi_lora/wrapper.rs.html#96-107)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/jammi_lora/wrapper.rs.html#96-107)

Insert this layer’s dropout-stream position keyed `{prefix}.dropout` into
`out`, if it has a dropout stream. No-op for `Frozen` and for a LoRA layer
with `lora_dropout == 0` (no stream to resume).

# should_apply_lora in jammi_lora - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-lora/0.32.1/jammi_lora/fn.should_apply_lora.html

```
pub fn should_apply_lora(
    module_name: &
```
[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    target_modules: &[[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)],
    layer_idx: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
    layers_to_transform: &[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>>,
) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)## Expand description

Decide whether a linear layer at `layer_idx` with name suffix `module_name`
should receive a LoRA adapter.

Semantics (mirroring HuggingFace PEFT):

- If `layers_to_transform`is`Some(ids)`,`layer_idx`must appear in it.
- If `target_modules`contains`"all-linear"`, match every layer name.
- Otherwise `module_name`must equal or end with one of the target strings.

# AdapterConfig in jammi_lora - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-lora/0.32.1/jammi_lora/struct.AdapterConfig.html

```
pub struct AdapterConfig {
    pub model_type:
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub lora_rank: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
    pub lora_alpha: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
    pub use_rslora: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    pub target_modules: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    pub layers_to_transform: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>>,
    pub rank_pattern: [HashMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/collections/hash/map/struct.HashMap.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>,
    pub backbone_dtype: [BackboneDtype](https://docs.rs/enum.BackboneDtype.html),
}## Expand description

Metadata describing a LoRA adapter injected into an encoder’s internal attention/FFN linears.

Persisted as JSON alongside `adapter.safetensors`. Discrimination between
different *kinds* of adapters (e.g. an external projection head vs. these
internal adapters) is a concern for the caller; this struct describes the
internal-adapter case only.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.model_type)

`model_type: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Backbone model family: e.g. `"bert"`, `"distilbert"`, `"modernbert"`.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.lora_rank)

`lora_rank: `[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)Default LoRA rank used at training time.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.lora_alpha)

`lora_alpha: `[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)LoRA scaling factor used at training time.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.use_rslora)

`use_rslora: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Whether RSLoRA-style `alpha / sqrt(rank)` scaling was used.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.target_modules)

`target_modules: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>Module-name suffixes that received a LoRA adapter.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.layers_to_transform)

`layers_to_transform: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>>Optional restriction of LoRA injection to specific layer indices.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.rank_pattern)

`rank_pattern: `[HashMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/collections/hash/map/struct.HashMap.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>Per-module rank overrides keyed by module-name substring.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.backbone_dtype)

`backbone_dtype: `[BackboneDtype](https://docs.rs/enum.BackboneDtype.html)Dtype used for the frozen backbone at training time. Defaults to F32.

Snapshot an `AdapterConfig` from a build-time `LoraBuildConfig`.

Run-time-only fields (`lora_dropout`, `init_mode`) are intentionally
not persisted — they affect training behaviour but do not change the
shape or semantics of the loaded adapter weights.

# save_adapter in jammi_lora - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-lora/0.32.1/jammi_lora/fn.save_adapter.html

`pub fn save_adapter<C: `[Serialize](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/ser/trait.Serialize.html)>(
    dir: &[Path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html),
    tensors: &[HashMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/collections/hash/map/struct.HashMap.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [Tensor](https://docs.rs/candle-core/0.9.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/candle_core/tensor/struct.Tensor.html)>,
    config: [&C](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [LoraError](https://docs.rs/enum.LoraError.html)>## Expand description

Write a LoRA adapter to `dir`:

- `adapter.safetensors`— the supplied- `tensors`map.
- `adapter_config.json`—- `config`serialised pretty as JSON.

Creates `dir` (and parents) if it does not exist. `config` can be any
[ Serialize](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/ser/trait.Serialize.html)-able type — typically

[when the adapter wraps encoder-internal linears, but callers with different adapter shapes can pass their own metadata struct or an enum that discriminates between shapes.](https://docs.rs/struct.AdapterConfig.html)

`AdapterConfig`

# load_adapter in jammi_lora - Rust
